newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN UNIONS ASK JOSPIN TO REVIEW RENAULT MOVE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN UNIONS ASK JOSPIN TO REVIEW RENAULT MOVE.

text.p: Trade union leaders at Renault's doomed Vilvoorde plant in Belgium on Sunday welcomed France's Socialist election win and called on the new government to honour promises to overturn the plant's closure.

The French daily newspaper Le Monde on Saturday quoted French Socialist leader and likely new prime minister Lionel Jospin as saying he would ask Renault to look for ways to keep the plant open if he won the election.
Renault said in February it would close the plant this year to streamline its European car assembly operations. The French state is Renault's largest shareholder, with 46 percent.

"I'm really pleased. This is a very important victory for all Europe's workers coming after Tony Blair's (Labour Party) election in Britain," Belga news agency quoted FGTB union official Karel Gacoms as saying.
"This gives us new hope for Vilvoorde. We hope the Socialist party will keep its promise to review the closure." REUTER 012005 GMT jun 97
